claim: [L21-L24,L37-L38,L49] (MED/incremental-dependencies) Included Fortran sources are declared as library dependencies instead of object dependencies, so edits can relink the library without recompiling the affected code.

[L18,L34,L40,L48,L51,L65-L74] (MED/parallel-build) The convenience library generates .lo objects while module targets request separate .o objects from the same sources, allowing competing module-file generation.

[L256-L260,L334-L335,L343-L350] (MED/incremental-dependencies) Included Fortran files are prerequisites of the archive rather than its compiled objects, so changing an include can relink stale object code.

[L76-L78,L343-L350,L496,L602-L605] (MED/parallel-build) Module targets trigger ordinary .o compilation while the library independently triggers .lo compilation of the same sources, allowing concurrent writes to the same module files.
[L221-L231] (MED/cache-key) All module names share ax_cv_fc_has_module, so subsequent module checks reuse the first module's result.
other_wording: [L220-L231] (MED/configure-cache) AX_FC_HAS_MODULE uses the single cache key ax_cv_fc_has_module for every module argument, so the result of the first module probe can be incorrectly reused for later different modules.

claim: [L218,L233-L236] (MED/output-contract) The module check defines a preprocessor symbol but never assigns the shell variable used by AM_CONDITIONAL or the documented FC_HAS_MODULE output.
other_wording: [L233-L236] (MED/configure-conditional) The macro defines HAVE_$1 via AC_DEFINE but tests the shell variable HAVE_$1 in AM_CONDITIONAL without assigning it, so the generated conditional can remain false even when the module probe succeeds.

claim: [L31,L50,L164,L183] (MED/cache-key) The repeatable line-length macros share one cache entry per language across different requested lengths and source formats.
[L1074-L1081] (MED/platform-version-matching) The Darwin undefined-symbol policy has no matching branch for explicit deployment targets beginning with 11 or later.
[L5157,L5862,L6731] (MED/variable-name) The OS/2 branches assign old_archive_From_new_cmds with an uppercase F instead of the declared old_archive_from_new_cmds variable.

[L6043-L6047,L7144-L7146,L7155-L7158,L7187-L7189] (LOW/platform-matching) Several branches match the full host triplet against bare sysv4 or osf3 patterns, preventing their intended platform-specific handling.
[L7537-L7538] (MED/dependency-parser) The separated -L and -R flag test prefixes only its left operands with x, so those flags cannot match and their following directory arguments are lost.
[L18-L19] (MED/build-order-coupling) The executable post-build deletes the entire shared distribution directory, including library DLLs published by the library post-build scripts.
[L22,L25-L26] (MED/stale-packaging) TargetDir is never cleared before wildcard packaging, allowing stale executables and DLLs from earlier builds to enter the new distribution.
[L20] (MED/stale-packaging) Adding into an existing ZIP does not remove entries whose source files disappeared, so repeated packaging can retain obsolete artifacts.

[L16,L20,L26] (LOW/packaging-side-effects) The script temporarily overwrites a destination 7za.exe and then deletes it unconditionally, with no distinction between its temporary copy and a pre-existing file.
[L68,L78,L148,L158] (MED/feature-configuration) Combined MPI_netcdf configurations omit feature preprocessor definitions despite compiling against libraries built with both features enabled.
other_wording: [L67-L78,L147-L158] (MED/configuration-contract) The MPI_netcdf configurations contain no PreprocessorDefinitions for USEMPI or USENETCDF, unlike the separate MPI and netcdf configurations, so their names do not match the feature flags they appear intended to enable.

claim: [L118,L148] (MED/configuration-contamination) x64 netCDF Release objects and MPI_netcdf Debug objects, modules, and PDB files are directed into Win32 directories.
other_wording: [L118] (MED/configuration-path) The netcdf_Release|x64 configuration writes object files to bin\win32\$(ConfigurationName) while its output/module paths are bin\x64, mixing architectures/configuration directories.

claim: [L130,L163] (MED/configuration-contamination) Several x64 configurations write objects or modules into Win32 output directories, creating architecture collisions.
other_wording: [L130] (MED/configuration-path) The netcdf_Release|x64 configuration writes object files to bin\win32\$(ConfigurationName) while its output/module paths are bin\x64, mixing architectures/configuration directories.

claim: [L75,L86,L163,L174] (MED/feature-configuration) Combined MPI_netcdf configurations enable preprocessing but omit MPI and netCDF definitions, unlike the corresponding static-library builds.
other_wording: [L74-L86,L162-L174] (MED/configuration-contract) The MPI_netcdf configurations contain no PreprocessorDefinitions for USEMPI or USENETCDF, unlike the separate MPI and netcdf configurations, so their names do not match the feature flags they appear intended to enable.

claim: [L85-L87] (LOW/error-propagation) SVN command failures occur inside successful echo recipes and can silently produce empty or invalid provenance fields.
other_wording: [L84-L87] (MED/reproducibility) version.dat is generated from live svnversion, svn info, and date commands with no fallback or command-failure handling, so builds outside an SVN checkout can produce empty metadata or fail depending on shell/error policy.

claim: [L84-L87] (MED/stale-provenance) version.dat has no prerequisites or forced refresh, so incremental rebuilds retain obsolete revision and build-date metadata.
[L111-L112] (MED/clean-rule) CLEANFILES includes every local *.inc file and therefore removes the distributed nh_pars.inc during an in-source clean.

[L6,L17-L18,L23-L29] (MED/build-order-coupling) Each library's post-build invocation republishes both libraries from fixed directories while ignoring TargetDir, allowing stale counterpart binaries or concurrent post-build interference.

[L8,L12-L15,L19] (MED/generated-file-location) The RevisionNumber branch writes version.dat in the working directory instead of includes/version/version.dat and marks success, leaving the compiler's version include stale or missing.
other_wording: [L11-L15,L18-L19] (MED/output-path) When RevisionNumber is defined the script writes version.dat in the current directory, whereas the normal and fallback paths target includes\version\version.dat, so the same script can produce metadata in different locations.

claim: [L13] (LOW/locale-dependence) Build_Date slices DATE at fixed character offsets, producing malformed dates under different Windows locale formats.
[L141] (MED/configuration-contamination) MPI_Debug|x64 writes modules into the win32 BMI directory.
other_wording: [L140-L142] (MED/configuration-path) MPI_Debug|x64 writes module files to bin\bmi\win32\$(ConfigurationName) while its output/object paths are x64, mixing architecture-specific module artifacts.
